newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian court can try former deputy premier.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian court can try former deputy premier.

text.p: Ethiopia's Supreme Court dismissed defence objections on Wednesday and ruled it could hear the trial of a former deputy prime minister accused of corruption.
It ordered the prosecution to amend charges against former deputy prime minister Tamirat Layne and eight businessmen to make them clearer and said it would resume hearings on July 30.
Defence lawyers had argued the supreme court under the penal code could not hear charges but should serve as an appeal court.

Tamirat, the former second-in-command in the government of Prime Minister Meles Zenawi, and the eight businessmen were charged by the state in March with corruption and abuse of power and face up to 15 years in jail each if they are found guilty.
Tamirat is accused of using his position to export 1,000 tonnes of state-owned coffee through a bogus firm for $3.6 million and taking $1.8 million of the proceeds for himself.
He has also been charged with fraudulently winning a tender for the supply of construction equipment. Tamirat was sacked as deputy prime minister last October and is held in "protective custody".
